targets.hook: 94% snaps, 18% target share three weeks running
targets.why: Otton has played 94% of Tampa Bay's snaps and drawn an 18% target share across all three weeks, a steady every-down TE role. The caveat is the quarterback: Baker Mayfield is out at least three weeks with a dislocated thumb and rookie Jalon Daniels starts (NFL.com, Sept. 28), which usually means shorter throws but fewer points.
targets.asset: Every-down TE with a sustained high-teens share; a weekly starter where targets are worth a full point each.
targets.rate_basis: recent-trend (wk 3): snap 94%, tgt 17%, 6 targets; wks 1-3 tgt 18%, snap 94%, 5.7 targets a game
targets.my_team_impact: Pat Freiermuth has a 13% share on 66% of snaps; Otton runs 18% on 94%. At a full point a catch that gap is worth starting Otton over Freiermuth now.
targets.confidence_why: Three-week sustained role (riser label 'window'); the rookie QB is the risk; med.

targets.hook: Miami's lead back now: 20 touches, 84% snaps in Wk 3
targets.why: De'Von Achane tore his ACL in Week 3 and is on season-ending IR (Dolphins, Sept. 28). Gordon took over: 17 carries for 41 yards and a TD plus 3 catches on 83-84% of snaps (CBS Sports, Sept. 28). Jaylen Wright (stinger, foot) is day-to-day and Malik Washington took some backfield snaps, so Gordon leads a committee rather than inheriting Achane's whole share. Efficiency was poor (2.4 a carry).
targets.asset: Volume-driven RB2/flex while he holds the early-down and goal-line work; touchdown-dependent until Wright is healthy.
targets.rate_basis: recent-trend (wk 3): snap 84%, touch share 30%, 20 touches, 3 RZ looks; wks 1-3 touch share 14% (backup before the injury)
targets.my_team_impact: A 20-touch lead back is a better Hall fill than your bench backs (Lloyd 7 touches on 23% of snaps in Week 3, Allgeier 6, White 9 with a sore shoulder). Claim both: the RB-needy count here is the highest of the three leagues.
